# `synchronized` - Wait and Notify

A bounded queue has two conditions: producers need space and consumers need an
item. Polling those conditions wastes CPU or adds arbitrary latency. Waiting in
a loop while *holding* the monitor is worse: the other side cannot acquire the
monitor to change the condition.

`wait()` solves that coordination problem. It releases the monitor and suspends
the current thread atomically. Another thread can then change the queue state
and call `notify()` or `notifyAll()` on the same monitor. An awakened thread
must reacquire the monitor before it can continue.

The monitor also provides the Java Memory Model visibility and ordering
guarantee used by this queue. A producer, consumer, or closer changes `queue` or
`closed` while holding the queue monitor, then exits its `synchronized` method.
That monitor unlock *happens-before* a later lock of the same monitor, including
the lock an awakened thread reacquires before returning from `wait()`. The
awakened thread therefore sees those protected state changes when it re-checks
its condition. `notify()` and `notifyAll()` provide coordination by making
waiters eligible to run; they do not themselves publish the state.

The condition must always be checked in a `while` loop:

```java
synchronized (lock) {
    while (conditionNotMet) {
        lock.wait();
    }

    /* The condition holds while this thread owns the monitor. */
}
```

A thread can wake spuriously, or another awakened thread can make the condition
false before this thread reacquires the monitor. The loop also makes it safe
when a notification occurs before a thread begins waiting: the state, rather
than the notification, determines whether it proceeds.

This queue uses `notifyAll()`. Producers and consumers wait on the same monitor
but for different conditions; `notify()` might wake a thread whose condition is
still false while a thread that could proceed remains asleep. `notifyAll()`
wakes every waiter, and each re-checks its condition. The trade-off is
unnecessary wake-ups and contention, so production code will usually prefer a
higher-level type such as `BlockingQueue`. The demo uses dedicated threads:
blocking the shared `ForkJoinPool` used by `CompletableFuture.runAsync()` can
delay unrelated tasks.

The program’s output is illustrative, not proof that a thread waited. Scheduling
can produce a valid run with neither waiting message. The tests establish a full
or empty queue, verify that the relevant worker is waiting, and then change the
queue state to release it.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this example, attendees can:

- explain why `wait()` must be called while holding the queue’s monitor and how
  it releases that monitor while waiting;
- use a condition loop to handle spurious wake-ups and competing waiters; and
- distinguish the liveness trade-off of `notifyAll()` from the
  condition-specific signalling provided by higher-level concurrency utilities.

## Prerequisite

Install a
[Oracle Java 8](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java8) JDK
or newer to compile and run this example. Ensure `java` and `javac` resolve to
Java 8 or newer in the terminal you use for the workshop.

## The program to inspect

`SharedQueue` is a bounded FIFO queue. Its `produce` and `consume` methods use
the queue instance’s monitor to protect state and wait until their respective
conditions hold.

The program uses one wait set for both queue conditions:

1. A producer waits while the queue is full, then adds an item and notifies the
   waiting threads.
2. A consumer waits while the queue is empty, then removes an item and notifies
   the waiting threads.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.Queue;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Numbers.requireGreaterThanZero;

public final class SharedQueue implements AutoCloseable {

    /* Protected by the synchronized(this) lock */
    private final Queue<Integer> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    private final int capacity;
    private boolean closed;

    public SharedQueue(final int capacity) {
        this.capacity = requireGreaterThanZero(capacity);
    }

    public synchronized void produce(final int value) {
        while (!closed && queue.size() >= capacity) {
            try {
                log("Queue is full. Producer is waiting...");
                wait(); /* Wait until space is available */
            } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                close();
                throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting", e);
            }
        }

        ensureOpen();
        queue.offer(value);
        log("Produced: " + value + " (size: " + queue.size() + ')');
        notifyAll(); /* Wake all waiters; each re-checks its condition */
    }

    public synchronized int consume() {
        while (!closed && queue.isEmpty()) {
            try {
                log("Queue is empty. Consumer is waiting...");
                wait(); /* Wait until an item is available */
            } catch (final InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                close();
                throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted while waiting", e);
            }
        }

        if (queue.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("The queue is closed");
        }

        final int value = queue.poll();
        log("Consumed: " + value + " (size: " + queue.size() + ')');
        notifyAll(); /* Wake all waiters; each re-checks its condition */
        return value;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized void close() {
        closed = true;
        notifyAll(); /* Wake waiters so they can observe the closed state */
    }

    public int capacity() {
        return capacity;
    }

    public synchronized boolean isEmpty() {
        return queue.isEmpty();
    }

    private void ensureOpen() {
        if (closed) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("The queue is closed");
        }
    }
}
```

`close` is this demo’s failure lifecycle. If `wait()` is interrupted, the queue
restores the interrupt status, closes itself, and fails that operation. Closing
wakes all waiters: producers fail immediately, while consumers drain any already
queued values and then fail once the queue is empty. This is a demo-specific
policy, not a replacement for a production cancellation design.

`Main` coordinates the two workers. It closes the queue if either worker fails,
waits for both workers, and reports the failure rather than printing a misleading
completion message. For normal completion, it sends a `NO_MORE_ENTRIES` poison
pill after the data. The marker reserves `-1` as a non-payload value and is only
suitable here because there is one consumer. With multiple consumers, the
producer would need one terminal marker per consumer, or a different explicit
completion protocol.

```java
package demo;

import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference;
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

import static demo.utils.Logs.log;
import static demo.utils.Logs.logHeaderAndJavaVersion;
import static demo.utils.Threads.sleepForAFewMilliseconds;
import static demo.utils.Threads.waitForAllThreadsToComplete;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) {
        logHeaderAndJavaVersion("Synchronized - Wait and Notify");

        final SharedQueue queue = new SharedQueue(5);
        final AtomicReference<RuntimeException> failure = new AtomicReference<>();

        log("Create Producer");
        final Thread producer = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                IntStream.concat(IntStream.rangeClosed(1, 10), IntStream.of(NO_MORE_ENTRIES) /* Used to signal to the consumer that there are not more elements */)
                        .peek(i -> {if (i > 6) {sleepForAFewMilliseconds();}})
                        .forEach(queue::produce);
            } catch (final RuntimeException e) {
                failure.compareAndSet(null, e);
                queue.close();
            }
        }, "producer");

        log("Create Consumer");
        final Thread consumer = new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                /* Keep reading from the queue until the NO_MORE_ENTRIES is read */
                for (int i; (i = queue.consume()) != NO_MORE_ENTRIES; ) {
                    log("Consumed " + i + " from the queue");
                }
            } catch (final RuntimeException e) {
                failure.compareAndSet(null, e);
                queue.close();
            }
        }, "consumer");

        producer.start();
        consumer.start();
        waitForAllThreadsToComplete(producer, consumer);
        if (failure.get() != null) {
            throw failure.get();
        }
        log("Completed");
    }

    private static final int NO_MORE_ENTRIES = -1;
}
```
